title: Exploring the Therapeutic Potential and Underlying Mechanism of Bergapten in Renal Fibrosis: Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation.
authors: Gairola, Shobhit; Saini, Montu; Bhatta, Archana; Kaundal, Ravinder K
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Bergapten抗肾纤维化作用，分子对接仅涉及小分子-蛋白，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterized by progressive interstitial fibrosis, contributing to high global mortality due to limited treatment options. Contemporary findings highlight the potential of natural compounds for CKD treatment. Bergapten (BGT), a bioactive furocoumarin, is recognized for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties but remains unexplored as an antifibrotic agent. The potential targets of BGT were identified using network pharmacology and in silico approaches. The antifibrotic effects of BGT were evaluated in transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1-induced normal rat kidney fibroblast (NRK-49F) cells. For in vivo validation, CKD was induced in mice using unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). Immunocytochemistry, histopathological analysis, and immunoblotting were conducted to assess the effects of BGT on fibroblast activation, renal microstructural changes, and expression of profibrotic markers. Network pharmacology analysis revealed 119 BGT-target genes involved in renal fibrosis, including those in the TGF-beta1 signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed the interaction of BGT with TGF-beta receptor 1 (TGFR1). In vitro studies demonstrated that BGT (30 muM) inhibited TGF-beta1-induced fibrotic response in NRK-49F cells by inhibiting TGF-beta1/Smad signaling. In vivo, oral administration of BGT (20 mg/kg) improved kidney function and alleviated histological damage, and pathological collagen deposition while mitigating renal inflammation. BGT suppressed the TGF-beta1/Smad signaling pathway, reduced the expression of extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins, and mitigated oxidative stress by activating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme-oxygenase-I (HO-I) signaling pathway. This study demonstrated the therapeutic potential of BGT in alleviating renal fibrosis in experimental models of CKD. The observed effects were attributed to the inhibition of TGF-beta1/Smad signaling and activation of the Nrf2 pathway.
abstract_zh: 慢性肾脏病（CKD）以进行性间质纤维化为特征，由于治疗选择有限，导致全球高死亡率。当代研究强调了天然化合物在CKD治疗中的潜力。Bergapten（BGT）是一种具有生物活性的呋喃香豆素，以其抗氧化和抗炎特性而闻名，但作为抗纤维化剂尚未被探索。利用网络药理学和计算机模拟方法鉴定了BGT的潜在靶点。在转化生长因子（TGF）-β1诱导的正常大鼠肾成纤维细胞（NRK-49F）中评估了BGT的抗纤维化效果。为进行体内验证，使用单侧输尿管梗阻（UUO）诱导小鼠CKD。通过免疫细胞化学、组织病理学分析和免疫印迹评估BGT对成纤维细胞活化、肾脏微结构变化及促纤维化标志物表达的影响。网络药理学分析揭示了119个参与肾纤维化的BGT靶基因，包括TGF-β1信号通路中的基因。分子对接确认了BGT与TGF-β受体1（TGFR1）的相互作用。体外研究表明，BGT（30 μM）通过抑制TGF-β1/Smad信号传导，抑制了TGF-β1诱导的NRK-49F细胞纤维化反应。在体内，口服BGT（20 mg/kg）改善了肾功能，减轻了组织学损伤和病理性胶原沉积，同时缓解了肾脏炎症。BGT抑制了TGF-β1/Smad信号通路，降低了细胞外基质（ECM）蛋白的表达，并通过激活核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）/血红素加氧酶-I（HO-I）信号通路减轻了氧化应激。本研究证明了BGT在CKD实验模型中缓解肾纤维化的治疗潜力。观察到的效应归因于TGF-β1/Smad信号传导的抑制和Nrf2通路的激活。
